A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 14-page versions of KAN-AD. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original detection and efficiency results, multivariate evaluations, ablations, and robustness experiments in Section 4.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results, including the univariate and multivariate evaluations in Tables 2 and 6.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 and Figure 3b's caption replace 'single-layer MLP' with 'linear layer.' Equation 12 already specifies the same affine projection in v3; the method components and multivariate adaptation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V4 adds NAB's Twitter subset and Yahoo to Appendix A.1, but still states that four datasets were selected. Tables 1–2 retain only KPI, TODS, WSD, and UCR, with no NAB/Yahoo results or statistics. Whether actual experimental coverage expanded is therefore unclear.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2, 3, and 6 and the case-study and robustness figures. No evaluated baseline is added or removed.

E3.justification: The reported splits, batch sizes, learning rate, 100-epoch maximum, metrics, and five-point detection-delay threshold are unchanged. No additional evaluation protocol accompanies the new appendix dataset descriptions.

E4.justification: The UCR case study, hyperparameter sweep, constant-term and function-family ablations, training-contamination robustness test, and Table 5 component ablations are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent trials with different random seeds and retain the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting for KAN-AD in Table 2.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results and graphical findings are unchanged, including average univariate Event F1 of 0.7798 in Table 2 and average multivariate Best F1 of 0.9076 in Table 6. No results accompany the added NAB/Yahoo descriptions.

T1.justification: The Kolmogorov–Arnold formulation, Fourier decomposition, and Equations 1–12 are mathematically unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same robustness, accuracy, parameter-efficiency, and inference-speed claims, including the stated four-benchmark evaluation.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning local-noise overfitting, Fourier smoothing, ablation outcomes, and multivariate applicability remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or qualification is added.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly identifies NAB's Twitter subset and describes Yahoo's data sources; the bibliography adds a Yahoo dataset-source URL. Existing implementation settings and KAN-AD code access remain unchanged. These additions do not establish additional experiments.

R1.justification: V4 adds Ahmad et al. (2017) for NAB and Research (2015) for Yahoo, with corresponding bibliography entries. The related-work discussion and methodological positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 corrects 'anoomaly,' clarifies the projection-layer terminology, changes several appendix references to section references, and adds two short dataset descriptions. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 3b's caption is corrected without changing the diagram. The figure and table set is retained; added references and appendix text cause modest reflow, including moving Appendix A.2's closing paragraph onto page 14.

improvement.justification: V4 clarifies the projection layer and adds source information, but Appendix A.1 now lists six datasets while still stating four, without corresponding NAB/Yahoo statistics or results. This makes the experimental scope less internally consistent. With the method and empirical evidence unchanged, this reporting inconsistency outweighs the small editorial gains.
